item: The window-history budget is pinned against the least tick row recorded when it was paid for, and a log with no closed window gives up no ticks
refs: PR #1477; follows PR #1464; Export's re-measure of #1464
summary: Export's independent re-measure of #1464 confirmed net zero before compression on five real logs and found two things. (1) The pin compared the windows with the tick the test builds (1,621 B), which is not the least a real tick is (1,552 B with the event-loop watchdog measuring, 1,478 B in target mode with no vitals), and which a coming tick trim would shrink under the pin although the zip would be smaller than before. The pin now compares 31 widest windows plus the member envelope (12,501 B) and 11 slim windows against the ticks given up at a RECORDED least maximum-mode tick of 1,552 B (production ticks measured 1,653 B or more; a target-mode no-vitals tick 1,478 B is the one paper case, named as not covered; the two keys that carry the windows are counted in the pin); the whole copy keeps 191 ticks instead of 192 (9 x 1,552 = 13,968 B), the slim copy 17 as before (3 x 1,552 = 4,656 B). (2) On a target-mode log the copies gave up 3 and 8 ticks for an empty windows member; a log with no closed window, or one that cannot be read, now keeps the ticks it kept before (20 and 200) and the member still says why it is empty (+about 138 B, not net zero by design: the reason is information), and the slim copy's collect_perf_newest_ticks reports the count used. Still uncompressed bytes: before compression only.
